long_biography.plain_text:
Langley began with equipment for Britain's coal industry, using assets left after his family's earlier engineering company collapsed. The new business adapted its products for steel, oil and gas customers before broadening into other engineering markets.

Its international scale came through acquisitions. Clarke Chapman added cranes and materials-handling systems, while later purchases brought cement equipment, electrical power systems, welding technology, packaging machinery, printing presses, motors and marine engines into the group. The current portfolio remains centred on capital equipment and power technologies for mission-critical industrial and digital infrastructure, including behind-the-meter generation for data centres.
